title: Private / federated mirror
description: Private and federated mirrors (spec 10863). A mirror is another registry root that this registry will federate resolution to, in `priority` order. The security property that makes federation safe is that a mirror CANNOT introduce trust: every entry it serves is still verified against the consumer's own trust policy and the publisher's own signature, so a hostile mirror can withhold a package or serve a stale one, but it cannot substitute a payload. `trust_mode` states which of those two weaker attacks the operator has accepted.

root.description: Filesystem root of the mirror, relative to the primary registry root. Local-only by construction: this build has NO network fetch, and a mirror that could name a URL would be a network fetch with extra steps. A remote transport is explicitly out of scope and recorded as such in MARKETPLACE-BUILD.md.

trust_mode.description: `verify-always`: accept a mirror entry on signature alone. `verify-and-require-primary-index`: additionally require the primary index to know the same (name, version, manifest_digest), which defeats a mirror serving a package the primary never published.
